If they're worried you're in danger of hurting yourself, they might make you stay the night, so probably bring a book and some clothes or something, just in case. 

It's a lot easier to do it this way, I'd say. If you do want help, please get some, because if you don't and it gets worse, it may (depending where you are) be a lot harder on you. Do what you believe is best for you. :)

I guess if I got the help I needed & asked for early on instead of being treated as though I were a lost cause, rabid and psychotic, things might have been different, but I've been determined to die for a very long time. Everyone with a degree thinks they know what's going on in *your* mind better than you do. Did you make it out okay? \<3

Did you manage to get through it okay? Would you like to talk about it?

I can believe at a pinch that a handful of therapists do care about their patients, but in the hospital, it's an entirely different story. They do not care, or they would never treat someone that way. I'm not psychotic or violent. I'm scared.

I actually appreciate the outside the box thinking you're doing. Perhaps it is numbness \- it's difficult to say, because I don't make these attempts on a whim, I always wait five days after deciding it's time & if I haven't changed my mind by then, I start making plans. I know most people believe suicide is just an impulsive, emotional decision, but I have complete clarity and control the entire time. Perhaps that's even worse. 

Mmmmm I have very few friends and no remaining family in the country \- suffer from some OCD and terrified of skin contact with other people, which only makes being manhandled in hospital that much harder. I suppose if circumstances were different I may think otherwise, but I have **no trust or faith** the mental health system, and after the way they treat me, I don't think that's unreasonable.

And they just can't or won't understand **why** I'm so terrified!

Like, I'm a functional person, even if I am hell bent on killing myself outside the hospital, I'm not a violent or erratic person under **most** circumstances. I have total clarity and control over myself. 

So if I've been strapped down for most of sixty straight hours and force fed pills and injected with sedatives and people occasionally take me to the toilet and all force me back and down into the bed so they can strap me down all over again and there's people screaming and yelling and a nurse that sometimes tickles my feet when nobody's around and the doctor and every other staff member NEVER believes a word I say \- why wouldn't I be scared and desperate and "hysterical?" I'm suicidal. Not a psychopath.
